Subject: Order form questions: invoice recipient + VAT treatment

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed. We started reviewing the Order Form and have two items blocking procurement:

1) Invoice recipient / remit-to: Our accounting team needs the invoice to be issued to Morpho Labs SAS (French entity) for EU VAT purposes. Can Redwood support invoicing to a second entity (Morpho Labs SAS) while the MSA remains with Morpho Labs, Inc.?

2) VAT treatment: Our tax team expects reverse-charge to apply on services; they will provide a VAT registration number but need a short clause in the Order Form confirming reverse-charge will be used when a valid VAT ID is supplied and that Redwood will not charge VAT in that case.

Also: procurement prefers Net 60 on the pilot tranche — is that something Redwood can accommodate, or do you require Net 30/45?

Attached our PO template for reference. If helpful, we can hop on a short call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Elena

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Order form questions: invoice recipient + VAT treatment — quick ops/legal ask

Neha / Karthik — quick tax guidance below: 

1) Reverse-charge evidence: a valid VAT registration number plus either the customer's EU VAT certificate or a link to VIES lookup confirming the VAT ID is active is fine. We should request the VAT ID in the PO and ask the customer to attach the VAT certificate where available.

2) Suggested Order Form language (concise):
"Taxes: Unless otherwise agreed in writing, Customer is responsible for all sales, use, value-added, and other taxes. If Customer provides a valid EU VAT registration number and applicable evidence, Customer shall be liable for VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism and Redwood will not charge VAT on the invoice"

3) Invoice entity: invoicing to Morpho Labs SAS is acceptable. Operational notes: we need the exact remit-to legal name, legal address, and VAT ID in the Order Form and the PO, and we will route invoices from our EU billing entity (Redwood Ireland Ltd.) when applicable.

4) Net terms: from a tax/timing perspective no blocker. Finance will need the PO to match remit-to. If we agree Net 60 for pilot, recommend one of: (a) 25% activation fee upfront, or (b) Net 60 with a $X credit hold clause (automatic offset on first invoice) — both mitigate receivable risk. Karthik to confirm pricing mechanics.

I've attached a short VAT evidence template you can send to the customer to collect their documents.

Kimberly Park
Director, Tax & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: VAT_Certificate_Form.xlsx (stub)

- VAT / reverse-charge: Redwood will honor reverse-charge where Morpho supplies a valid VAT registration number and evidence. Please attach the VAT certificate (or confirmation from VIES) when returning the PO.
- Net terms: We can accept Net 60 for the pilot provided a 25% activation fee is paid upfront (applies to the pilot tranche only). If you'd prefer no upfront, we can instead apply Net 60 with a small credit hold; Karthik, who is cc'd, can finalize the dollar treatment.
- Next steps: I attached the redlined Order Form (Redline_OrderForm_v2.pdf) with the invoice remit block and our suggested VAT clause. If that looks good, please: (1) confirm remit-to details in reply, (2) attach VAT evidence, and (3) issue a PO referencing deal MORPHO-2027-042.
